reader_copy.en: When Holy Week church bells fell silent, children in parts of Austria went through villages sounding wooden ratchets called Ratschen and singing verses to announce prayer times and recall Christ's Passion.
reader_copy.fr: Quand les cloches se taisaient pendant la Semaine sainte, des enfants parcouraient les villages de certaines régions d'Autriche avec des crécelles en bois appelées Ratschen, chantant des couplets pour annoncer la prière et rappeler la Passion du Christ.

source_links.title: Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

locator.passage: Ratschenbuben ... commemorate the events of Christ's Passion

source_links.title: Austrian UNESCO Commission — Ratschen during Holy Week

scope.religious_context: Holy Week; lay/customary practice, not a universal rubric

reader_copy.en: At Saint Dominic's Priory in Valletta, Malta, a Holy Week Last Supper table has been prepared since 1784. Its food was traditionally given to poor families after Good Friday, joining the commemoration to charity.
reader_copy.fr: Au prieuré Saint-Dominique de La Valette, à Malte, une table de la Cène est préparée pendant la Semaine sainte depuis 1784. Autrefois, les aliments étaient distribués aux familles pauvres après le Vendredi saint, associant la commémoration à la charité.

source_links.title: Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

locator.passage: In Malta, a Last Supper Table is richly laden by the faithful with food that is later distributed to the poor

source_links.title: Times of Malta — Last Supper table at St Dominic’s, Valletta

scope.religious_context: Holy Week Catholic charity table, not the Eucharistic rite
scope.current_practice: Historical distribution after Good Friday documented; current arrangements may differ

reader_copy.en: In medieval western Europe, Saint Martin's Day on 11 November often marked harvest thanksgiving. People first attended Mass, then celebrated their filled barns with games, processions and a festive dinner.
reader_copy.fr: Dans l'Europe occidentale médiévale, la Saint-Martin du 11 novembre marquait souvent l'action de grâce pour les récoltes. Après la messe, on célébrait les granges remplies par des jeux, des défilés et un repas de fête.

source_links.title: Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

locator.passage: People first went to Mass and observed the rest of the day with games, dances, parades, and a festive dinner

scope.religious_context: local harvest thanksgiving associated with Saint Martin, not universally prescribed Mass custom

reader_copy.en: In Valencia, the Fallas festival culminates on 19 March, Saint Joseph's Day, when towering satirical figures are burned. The celebration is traditionally linked to carpenters honouring their patron, though its exact origins are debated.
reader_copy.fr: À Valence, la fête des Fallas culmine le 19 mars, jour de la Saint-Joseph, par l'embrasement de grandes figures satiriques. On la rattache traditionnellement aux menuisiers honorant leur patron, bien que ses origines exactes soient discutées.

source_links.title: Handbook of Christian Feasts and Customs (1958)

locator.passage: the best one receives a prize ... others are burned in joyful bonfires ... in honor of Saint Joseph

scope.religious_context: civic festival aligned with Saint Joseph's patronal feast, not a Catholic liturgical rite
